changes: Lālaratna: roles changed from scribe+beneficiary to scribe+owner (he copied it 'adhyayanāya', for (his) study; no separate beneficiary)
Date: 'hy anaḍuhi' read as sun in Taurus (Vṛṣa); month 'śukra' = Jyeṣṭha; paksa normalised to śukla; tithi pratipad from 'sitādime' (tentative); weekday Wednesday from 'jñe 'hni' (written 'jenhi')
Purpose corrected: colophon has only 'adhyayanāya'; the 'bhūsurāṇām' in the first reading is not in the text ('bhūsuro 'lam' describes the scribe)
Notes expanded on the corrupt date phrase

purpose: adhyayanāya (for study, presumably the scribe's own)
notes: The chronogram, read right to left, is rasa 6, nigama 4, haya 7, indu 1, giving ŚS 1746 (about 1824 CE). 'gahaya' is a corruption of 'haya'. I take the corrupt date phrase as 'śākake 'rke hy anaḍuhi śukra-sitādime (?) jñe 'hni': the year in the Śaka era, the sun in Taurus, the month Śukra (= Jyeṣṭha), the first day of the bright fortnight, a Wednesday. The tithi and weekday readings are conjectural; I have not checked them against an ephemeris. Trinayanapurī ('city of the three-eyed one', i.e. Śiva) means Kāśī/Vārāṇasī, which fits the closing invocation to Viśveśvara. It could equally be the scribe's home rather than the place of copying. 'bhūsuro 'lam' marks Lālaratna as a brahmin. The catalogue's scribe field (Lālaratna Śarmā) agrees.
